evidence.quote: From {{inh|en|enm|striden}}, from {{inh|en|ang|strīdan|t= stride}}, from {{inh|en|gmw-pro|*strīdan}}, from {{der|en|gem-pro|*strīdaną}}.<ref>{{R:Etymonline}}</ref> Cognate with {{cog|nds|striden||to fight, to stride}}, {{cog|nl|strijden||to fight}}, {{cog|de|streiten||to fight, to quarrel}}.

"to straddle, mount" (a horse), from Proto-Germanic *stridanan (source also of Middle Low… See origin and meaning of stride. from Old English stridan (past tense strad , past participle striden ), "to straddle, mount" (a horse), from Proto-Germanic *stridanan (source also of Middle Low German strede "stride, strive;" Old Saxon stridian , Danish stride , Swedish strida "to fight," Dutch strijden , Old High German stritan , German s treiten "to fight, contend, struggle," Old Norse striðr "strong, hard, stubborn, severe").
